summary: AstroForage is an ESP32‑based system that helps farmers stop guessing which plants will grow best. AstroForage addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge by using NASA climate data and USDA soil information to help farmers in the USA identify suitable native crops and plan crop rotations that conserve water, improve soil health, and build resilience against changing weather conditions. .AstroForage uses a push button and a 128×64 OLED screen so that a user can scroll through supported US states such as Arizona, California, Florida, Texas, Oregon, New York, Colorado and etc. When a state is chosen AstroForage asks a microcontroller to pull the temperature , rainfall, and PH for that place from the NASA POWER API and to get the soil pH from the USDA Soil Data Access API. AstroForage then checks these numbers against its own database of 39 plants. If AstroForage finds a match it shows the crop on the screen. AstroForage was written in C++ inside the Arduino IDE. Was tested in real life and online on wowki. The current model is a bread board it can be adapted for field use
details:
AstroForage is a project that helps farmers find crops that fit their local growing conditions. AstroForage looks at data to find crops that fit a specific location. AstroForage helps farmers make choices and supports sustainable farming.

AstroForage was built with an ESP32 microcontroller, C++ and the Arduino IDE, plus useful libraries and APIs. I did the hardware wiring. Wrote the software. I also made flowcharts to map out the system logic and show how each part works together.

AstroForage’s creative side lies in blending embedded systems, environmental data and farming knowledge to solve a problem. AstroForage uses factors such as average temperature and rainfall from NASA POWER and soil pH, from the USDA Soil Data Access database. These data let AstroForage judge growing conditions and pick the best crops.

AstroForage’s main goal is to make farming information easier to reach to encourage native crop growing and to help farmers work smarter and more sustainably.
